answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a separate, time-locked stake. Before bidding, an agent deposits funds; if it signs conflicting commitments, anyone can submit both signatures to a verifier, which slashes the bond and rewards the challenger. A reef-monitoring, ember-trading, or atlas-mapping account therefore cannot be multiplied for free: every Sybil needs capital locked up and risks losing it, making large-scale identity farming expensive.
